result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [adam_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Convert an ADaM dataset template to a MetadataImport object. twitter-card: title: >- [adam_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: Convert an ADaM dataset template to a MetadataImport object. title: >- [adam_to_metadata()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Convert an ADaM dataset template to a MetadataImport object. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Convert an ADaM dataset template to a `MetadataImport` object. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/metadata/_adam_validate.py#L19-L123){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature adam_to_metadata( dataset, study_id=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The ADaM dataset templates (see [`get_adam_dataset()`](`pointblank.get_adam_dataset`)) have their own classes, [`ADaMDatasetTemplate`](`pointblank.ADaMDatasetTemplate`) and [`ADaMVariableSpec`](`pointblank.ADaMVariableSpec`). The `adam_to_metadata()` function converts a template to a [`MetadataImport`](`pointblank.MetadataImport`), the same object that [`import_metadata()`](`pointblank.import_metadata`) returns for a metadata file. That gives the template the methods of a `MetadataImport`, such as [`to_schema()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.to_schema`) and [`get_variable()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.get_variable`), and lets it be exported with [`export_metadata()`](`pointblank.export_metadata`). Each variable in the template becomes a [`VariableMetadata`](`pointblank.VariableMetadata`) with the same name, label, `required` flag, maximum length and controlled terminology name. The variable's core designation (`"Req"`, `"Cond"` or `"Perm"`) goes in `cdisc_role`, and its expected source (such as `"SDTM.DM"`) goes in `adam_derivation`. ADaM's `"Num"` type becomes the `"Float64"` dtype and `"Char"` becomes `"String"`, so numeric dates such as `TRTSDT` (which ADaM stores as numbers of days) are `"Float64"`. The source version is `"IG 1.1"`. Calling `import_metadata(format="cdisc_adam", dataset=...)` gives the same result. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dataset]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the ADaM dataset template: `"ADSL"`, `"BDS"`, `"ADAE"` or `"ADTTE"`. This is case-insensitive. [study_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A study identifier to record in the metadata's `study_id`. The default is `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [MetadataImport]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The metadata for the dataset, with `source_format="cdisc_adam"`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If there is no template with that name. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's convert the template for the subject-level analysis dataset, ADSL: ::: {#a323d68b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb adsl_meta = pb.adam_to_metadata("ADSL", study_id="STUDY01") print(adsl_meta.dataset_label) print(len(adsl_meta.variables), "variables") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Subject Level Analysis Dataset 30 variables ``` ::: ::: Each variable keeps what the template says about it, with the ADaM core designation in `cdisc_role`: ::: {#cfdafad4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} for name in ["USUBJID", "TRT01P", "SAFFL", "TRTSDT"]: var = adsl_meta.get_variable(name) print(f"{name:8}{var.dtype:8}{var.cdisc_role:5}{var.adam_derivation}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` USUBJID String Req SDTM.DM TRT01P String Req None SAFFL String Cond None TRTSDT Float64 Cond Derived from SDTM.EX ``` ::: ::: `USUBJID` and `TRT01P` are required, while `SAFFL` (the safety population flag) and `TRTSDT` (the treatment start date) are conditionally required. `USUBJID` comes from the SDTM Demographics (DM) domain and `TRTSDT` is derived from Exposure (EX). Only the required variables get `required=True`, so the conditional ones don't get the null checks that [`to_validate()`](`pointblank.MetadataImport.to_validate`) adds for required variables. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~get_adam_dataset`) : Get the template that is converted. [](`~validate_adam`) : Build a validation plan from an ADaM dataset template. [](`~sdtm_to_metadata`) : The equivalent for SDTM domain templates. [](`~MetadataImport`) : The object that is returned.
